Replay

Replay Godot integration

9 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Choose an importThe lifecycle

Session(State, Control, Action, Event, Seats) owns the routine local/network lifecycle around the engine-free runner. The application supplies a typed model, initial frame, options, sampled controls/actions, and presentation.

Choose an import#

Package Import alias Owns
godot:replay/godot replaygd Session, Party, Room, enrollment, recovery and their checkpoint operations
godot:replay/godot/scene scenegd Scene/view pools, typed script bindings, baking, resources, effects, audio and body adapters
godot:replay/godot/input inputgd Device bindings, captured controls, signal actions and tracked action intents
godot:replay/godot/storage storagegd Files, browser stores, persistent profiles, tokens and archive encoding
godot:replay/godot/transport transportgd Direct ENet, RTC, Steam and WebSocket adapters
godot:replay/godot/debug debuggd Optional overlays, history inspection, recording, playback and telemetry

Start with the root import for a Session or Room. Its selected transport is managed internally; using Session does not require driving a transport adapter. Add a feature import when the game uses that feature's owners directly. Scene, input and debug packages extend the lifecycle package. Storage and transport are independent foundations. The internal wire helpers are implementation details shared by the lifecycle and transport packages.

Migrating the earlier single-package API#

Types and procedures retain their names in their owning feature package. Add that import and change the qualifier, for example replaygd.Script_View to scenegd.Script_View, replaygd.Enet to transportgd.Enet, and replaygd.storage_read to storagegd.storage_read. Generated scene descriptors use the scene package automatically after regeneration. The root package does not re-export feature APIs; old qualified names fail compilation.

session_open, session_frame, session_close and the Party/Room lifecycle stay at root. Session-specific Browser_Checkpoint also stays at root because it checks the live Session's authority, identity and recovery policy; it uses the storage package for I/O.

The lifecycle#

Start with a zero-initialized owner and copy SESSION_OPTIONS for its settings; an empty Session_Options{} does not contain the network defaults. Keep the live owner at a stable address, usually a field on the game's Godot script. Call session_close from that script's exit lifecycle. Do not copy an open Session or defer its close in _ready, which would close it as soon as _ready returns.

Task Normal API
Direct local or authoritative game session_open, session_frame, session_close
Submit a discrete action session_issue; add input intents when retaining and tracking a pending action
Read presentation Drain session_changes, then read the copied session_state
Invitations and durable enrollment party_open, party_begin, party_frame, party_room_options, party_close
Coordinator-owned recovery room_open, room_frame, room_issue, room_close; read changes/state through room.session

Use one Session or Room owner for a game. Room owns its Session and drives it; do not call session_frame separately on room.session. Party remains alive while Room borrows its authorization. Close Room before Party and its storage.

Editor-first authoring connects ordinary scene-local scripts to typed display values. Replay Scrapyard is the canonical composition example, with standalone actor/HUD previews and validated Resource baking.

Typed view pools bind generation-safe entity projections to cached Godot child references and skip unchanged property writes.

Definition baking converts authored Resources and scene markers to validated immutable values with content identity and retained versions. Further boundary work is tracked in the bridge plan.

Local diagnostic overlay adds optional runtime counters and explicit recent-history audits without game-specific reporting code.

Local history inspection adds a retained-frame slider with explicit resume/branch commands and validated scalar edits to a copied preview. Replay Hello demonstrates pause, historical views, input guards and a new presentation epoch for an alternate local future.

Portable local recordings export replayable gameplay windows from the history dock and verify them in a separate headless process. Loaded recording playback opens those files in Godot, shows recorded frames and mismatch details, and returns explicit branch commands.

Explicit body contracts distinguish World-driven bodies from authority-gated cooperative Godot solver observations.

Declarative effect routes bind events to typed scene/paint callbacks or sound cues with bounded lifetime and rollback handling.

Bounded event audio consumes presentation changes with retained one-shot IDs and bounded Godot voice pools.

Steam packet transport adds an explicit Session backend with separate contract, native-capability and live-account acceptance gates.

Connection generations distinguish successive MultiplayerPeer connections and fence queued data when numeric IDs are reused.

Browser identities and local checkpoints add persistent credentials, validated archive loading and save completion receipts.

Browser blob storage provides asynchronous commit receipts and revision-checked IndexedDB writes for local identities, profiles and serialized data. Storage runs outside the simulation contract.

Odin
options := replaygd.SESSION_OPTIONS
options.role = .Host // Solo, Host, Server, Client, Observer
options.network.hz = 20
error := replaygd.session_open(&session, initial_frame, model, options)
if error != .None {
	replaygd.session_close(&session)
	return error
}

// Each frame: sample devices outside simulation.
error = replaygd.session_frame(&session, delta_seconds, controls)
if error != .None {
	return error
}
for {
	count := replaygd.session_changes(&session, changes[:])
	if count == 0 {
		break
	}
	for change in changes[:count] {
		present_change(change) // Application presentation callback.
	}
}
frame, valid := replaygd.session_state(&session)
if valid {
	present_state(frame.state) // Application presentation callback.
}

session_issue routes a local player's action to the authority or predicting client. Consume session_changes before the next frame. It carries gameplay effects and action verdicts; an authoritative verdict is a Confirm, or a change whose confirmed flag is set. Simulation never renders or accesses device state. The facade drains the lower-level duplicate outcome convenience queue so normal games have one presentation-consumer door.

The caller supplies the changes scratch array. Drain until zero even when that array is smaller than the pending batch; leaving changes queued makes the next session_frame return .Presentation. The checked lifecycle recipes show this complete loop with concrete types.

Typed InputMap and signal bindings buffer tick edges, apply explicit pause/focus/menu gates and capture copied UI actions.

Copied action intents retain a pending payload through submission failure and track epoch-scoped tickets through confirmation and recovery. They provide the common latch/result bookkeeping without changing gameplay policy.

For mixed local/remote presentation, supply Model.event_owner and set options.remote_observed=true. Local effects remain speculative; remote effects wait for the observed clock. The option survives Room promotion, redirection and old-host rejoin. Bind aiming input to the displayed remote frames using net.client_present. This changes presentation policy; the default runner predicts the complete public world. Model.group can opt into an authored closed group; see prediction groups.

scenegd.Nodes2 maintains bounded scene instances by presentation identity, with retained scene ownership. scenegd.nodes_get supports game-specific dressing of child nodes. scenegd.scene_instance loads/instances an authored stage and releases the temporary resource reference. inputgd.bind_key/inputgd.bind_mouse release constructor references after InputMap retains the events. storagegd.session_token uses random credentials normally; deterministic labels are for tests. storagegd.session_profile(path) creates or reads a persistent local token. Use a separate profile for each player running on one machine; malformed existing profiles fail instead of silently changing identity.

session_save(session, path) captures and writes a complete authority archive. storagegd.checkpoint_read validates one against the game's model/content, and session_resume opens a fresh authority using explicit newer-epoch/local-seat options. Host/solo resume verifies that the profile token owns the selected seat. Writes close a flushed staging file before replacing the destination. Existing archives survive an interrupted next write; power-loss durability and browser filesystem persistence have not been verified. One writer may own a path at a time.

The separate Cavecrawl save gate kills its writer and resumes in a fresh process; the co-op recovery gate replaces both host and guest and checks stable-seat loot and continued actions. See recovery for API examples and the distinction between local recovery and the Room migration driver.

Network sessions now share an ENet connection between gameplay and checkpoint replication through recovery.Link. To accept complete authority backups, set options.replication.accept_checkpoints=true before opening a client. On the authority, session_backup_seat(session, seat, interval_ticks) explicitly authorizes that admitted player as a recipient. session_frame handles routing, periodic capture, chunk repair, validation, and combined traffic budgets. The default interval is one simulation second. session_backup_receipt reports a validated receipt; session.link.error and model_error report backup failures without stopping play.

This authorization discloses authority-only state. It does not make the recipient an elected host. Connection replacement requires explicit authorization of the new live binding. The Room driver adds coordinator fencing and tested surviving-client takeover; broader M5 cases remain open.

The authority model and permit enforcement are now available in replay/authority. For a leased session, set options.network.require_permit=true and supply options.permit. session.fenced reports an expected pause when it is unavailable; fixed-step backlog is discarded while fenced. The application must continue its coordinator/UI loop separately. The authenticated decision service and durable store are now available, along with the initial Room takeover driver. See the service contract.

The facade is experimental. It supports full-public and authored group prediction with the existing ENet/fault adapters. Room now adds coordinator-driven planned and crash migration with surviving-client reconnection in tested Cavecrawl and Quickdraw combat scenarios. Session communications adds optional bounded chat and markers through an independent application lane. Owner-streamed physics has separate 2D and 3D adapters. Matchmaking and a complete lobby UI remain roadmap work rather than implicit guarantees of the convenience wrapper.

For direct sessions, Session_Options.discover_epoch=true enables a small pre-join query of the selected host. It discovers the current epoch before the strict Hello/Welcome exchange, so a fresh client can join a manually resumed host. It must be enabled on both endpoints, defaults off, and is rejected for leased sessions. It neither elects nor authenticates the host. The network contract describes challenge matching, timeout and scope restrictions. Room continues to obtain authority epochs from its coordinator.

Session_Options.reuse_equal_corrections opts a client into the core's exact correction-reuse path. It defaults off and requires stable deterministic step semantics. client.stats.reused_correction_ticks reports retained records while replayed_ticks counts simulated correction steps. It changes local work only, not snapshot cadence, packet contracts or authoritative validation. Mixed Scrapyard initially exposes few matching records, so this is not enabled by default as a universal performance improvement.

Session.control_consumed reports whether the supplied control was used by an actual local/authority input step during the last session_frame call. It is false when there was no prepared tick, prediction is blocked, a snapshot merely moves or bootstraps the timeline, or the role does not consume local controls. Use this receipt to clear pending device edges; a larger timeline head alone does not prove input was sampled. The field resets at each Session or Room frame call, including early returns. It is not an authority acceptance or delivery acknowledgment.

Odin
error = replaygd.session_frame(&session, dt, control)
if session.control_consumed {replay.buttons_consume(&buttons)}

Immutable procedural polygons can use mesh2_polygon, with ordinary Godot node transforms and instance tint for animation.

Room clients can display recovery-backup status, including approval, freshness and uncertainty, without using UI state as authority permission.

For short linear visual motion, session_tick_phase feeds a caller-owned view.Tick_Phase after Session/Room advances. Prediction stalls and fencing cannot turn a wrapped fixed-clock fraction into backward render motion. Gameplay membership and collision decisions remain in the model.

Room moderation queues durable enrolled-member removal and tracks its result, preserving bans through successor replacement and old-checkpoint recovery. Direct Session bans retain their checkpoint durability contract.

Steam Room destinations use explicit authenticated endpoint encoding and fresh peer construction through recovery. Local contract acceptance is recorded separately from still-pending live multi-account Steam validation.

Typed archetype registries and scene pools connect stable gameplay IDs and baked definitions to independently authored local scenes and appearances.

Typed scene adapters and optional view codegen provide owned script/archetype bindings, permanent scene bindings, scope tracking, typed visitation, contextual errors and checked Resource/bake helpers.
